rules.statement: Register a library's default implementation of a service with `TryAdd*` (for example `TryAddSingleton`), not `Add*`, so a host that registers its own implementation first replaces it.
rules.why: The ADR registers the default resolver with `TryAddSingleton` so a host can replace the resolution in one place by registering its own before the library.
rules.check: Look for library DI extension methods that register a default service implementation with `AddSingleton`/`AddScoped`/`AddTransient` instead of the `TryAdd` variants.

rules.statement: Read `IOptions`/`IOptionsMonitor` values when they are used, not in a service's constructor.
rules.why: Reading options on use keeps construction free of dependencies, so services on the path that builds a shared root object don't form a dependency cycle and see current values.
rules.check: Look for constructors that read `.Value` or `.CurrentValue` (or `Get(name)`) from injected options and store the result in a field.

rules.statement: Code that must see a write just committed, such as a seed, a preview or a validation of a proposed change, reads the committed record from the store, not a cached copy that a replica refreshes by polling.
rules.why: On the replica that committed a change, the polled copy may not be refreshed yet, so it would give a stale answer.
rules.check: Look for seeds, previews or checks that run after a write and read a polled or cached provider when the store holds the authoritative record.

rules.statement: Don't return an ETag or concurrency token on an HTTP response that shows a merged or computed view across several entities.
rules.why: A merged view isn't an entity that can be written back, so a token has nothing to guard.
rules.check: Look for read-only merged, effective or preview endpoints that set an ETag header or include a version or concurrency token in the body.

rules.statement: A management endpoint that previews derived data authorizes the same permission as the raw read of that resource, and does so before it resolves or computes anything.
rules.why: Resolving only after authorization avoids doing work for, and leaking information to, callers who don't have authority, and the preview gets no weaker protection than the raw data.
rules.check: Look for preview or derived-view handlers that resolve data before the authorization check, or that require a different or weaker permission than the raw read endpoint.

rules.statement: Don't add an anonymous override or query option to a public discovery endpoint that exposes settings marked non-discoverable. Expose them only through an authorized management endpoint.
rules.why: An anonymous override would disclose settings to callers who don't have authority.
rules.check: Look for discovery or metadata endpoints gaining a parameter or flag that includes non-discoverable values without authorization.

rules.statement: Compute a scope's effective settings (the cascade merge plus security-profile expansion) through the single effective-settings resolver service, never with a merge written by hand in the caller.
rules.why: Hand-written copies drift: they read the platform from different sources and some skip the profile expansion, so they give a different answer than the runtime.
rules.check: Look for new code that merges platform, team, tenant or client settings documents itself, or that deserializes a settings document without going through the resolver.
